Improvisation 27 (Garden of Love II)

Wassily Kandinsky, 1912

Oil on canvas

Loose abstract shapes in soft reds, yellows and greens on a pale ground.

Use this style

Wassily Kandinsky, Improvisation 27 (Garden of Love II), 1912. Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York. Source on Wikimedia Commons. Licence: CC0.

About the painting

Kandinsky sorted his paintings of these years into three kinds: Impressions, taken from nature; Improvisations, largely unconscious and spontaneous; and Compositions, worked out slowly. Improvisation 27 was painted in Munich in 1912, when he was leading the Blaue Reiter group with Franz Marc.

It was shown at the 1913 Armory Show in New York, where the photographer Alfred Stieglitz bought it. It came to the Metropolitan Museum of Art with his collection in 1949, and the museum publishes this image under CC0. Patches of red, yellow and blue float on a pale ground, held together by quick black lines.

How it looks on your photo

A light, muted look. The model spreads soft red, yellow and slate-blue patches over the photo and adds loose dark strokes, while the shapes underneath mostly stay readable. It suits gardens, interiors and anything you want to look playful rather than dramatic.
